# Requirements Quality Checklist: ShelfHelp Shared Core

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, completeness, and internal consistency of the shared core requirements (decisions, policies, domain model, gating, NFRs, data model) that all 20 feature specs depend on.
**Created**: 2025-10-25
**Feature**: [000-core/spec.md](../spec.md) — with authority delegated to `specs/SHELFHELP_FULLSPEC.md` §3, §4, §12, §13, §15.2

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Scope, Precedence & Traceability

- [ ] CHK001 - Is the precedence order (SRS §3/§4 → PA1 → agent judgment) stated once and applied consistently, rather than restated with subtle variation across sections? [Consistency, Spec §Preamble] — *PASS: stated once in the preamble; `docs/DECISIONS.md` applies it. Feature specs reference, not restate.*
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the boundary between this core doc and the authoritative SRS explicit about which section wins when both define the same rule? [Clarity, Spec §Preamble, §8, §9] — *PASS: preamble states SRS §3/§4 win; §8/§9 explicitly delegate detail to SRS §12/§15.2.*
- [ ] CHK003 - Are all requirement IDs defined by a single ID scheme with no collisions across groups (FR/DEC/POL/NFR/TS/EC/ASM/RISK)? [Traceability, Spec §ID scheme] — *PASS: one scheme in the preamble; verified no duplicate FR IDs across the 20 split specs.*
- [ ] CHK004 - Is it documented what happens to a requirement when it is retired, and is ID reuse explicitly prohibited? [Completeness, Spec §ID scheme, Constitution Principle VIII] — *PASS: Constitution Principle VIII and SRS §20 state retired IDs are never reused.*
- [ ] CHK005 - Are the SHALL/SHOULD/MAY keywords used consistently, with every SHOULD accompanied by a recorded-reason expectation? [Clarity, Spec §Keywords] — *PASS: keywords defined in the preamble (SHALL/SHOULD/MAY) with the SHOULD = expected-unless-recorded-reason rule; core is policy prose, so few SHOULDs occur.*
- [ ] CHK006 - Is it specified how a downstream feature spec is expected to cite core (by ID vs by section number), so references cannot rot when core is edited? [Ambiguity, Gap] — *OPEN: feature specs cite both forms (e.g. "POL-07", "§5.3"). No stated rule. Low severity, but section-number citations will rot if core is renumbered; consider mandating ID-only citations.*

## Scope Boundaries & Out-of-Scope Handling

- [ ] CHK007 - Is "out of scope" (§1.4) expressed as testable negatives rather than a prose list, so a reviewer can confirm a feature is genuinely excluded? [Measurability, Spec §1.4] — *OPEN: §1.4 is a prose list. Each exclusion is checkable in principle (e.g. "real payment gateway" = only a simulator exists) but none is written as an acceptance condition. Minor.*
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the §20 archived features referenced with enough detail that a reviewer can tell they are not accidentally re-specified in a feature doc? [Consistency, Spec §12] — *OPEN: core only points at SRS §20 by name. §20 carries per-feature detail, so the check is possible but requires leaving core. Acceptable given core is a summary.*
- [ ] CHK009 - Is it defined whether an archived feature's ID may be referenced in a new requirement without implying reinstatement? [Ambiguity, Gap] — *OPEN: Constitution Principle VIII prohibits ID reuse but is silent on *referencing* an archived ID. Real but low-impact ambiguity; worth one sentence.*

## Glossary & Terminological Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 - Does every domain term used normatively (Book, Copy, Member, Charge, Payment, Receipt, Debt hold, Restricted, Strike) appear in the glossary? [Completeness, Spec §1.5] — *PASS: all nine terms are defined in the §1.5 glossary.*
- [ ] CHK011 - Are glossary definitions consistent with the state machines in §5 (e.g. "Receipt" described as immutable in the glossary matches POL-10 and FR-RCPT-06)? [Consistency, Spec §1.5 vs §5, §4.10] — *PASS: glossary calls Receipt "immutable ledger row"; POL-10 and FR-RCPT-06 enforce insert-only. Consistent.*
- [ ] CHK012 - Is the distinction between "Loan Request" and "Loan Item" defined unambiguously enough to decide which entity a status belongs to? [Clarity, Spec §1.5, §5.2] — *PASS: glossary separates Request (grouping + pickup deadline/payment) from Item (the status-bearing unit); §5.2 is titled "Loan Item states".*
- [ ] CHK013 - Is "Member" defined relative to a point in time, and is the boundary condition at membership expiry (last day vs next day) explicit? [Clarity, Spec §1.5, POL-03] — *PASS: glossary says "active membership at the current time"; POL-03 statuses are date-derived and FR-MEM-05 resolves at a point in time. Boundary is `end_at` inclusive.*

## Decisions Register Quality

- [ ] CHK014 - Does every DEC row state both the issue and a concrete adopted resolution, rather than deferring with "TBD" or a restated question? [Completeness, Spec §3] — *PASS: all 56 rows have Issue + Adopted resolution; no TBDs.*
- [ ] CHK015 - Are all rows marked `Confirm = Yes` traceable to an owner sign-off action, and is the consequence of shipping without sign-off defined? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §3] — *OPEN: ~40 rows are `Confirm = Yes`, but no owner, sign-off record, or consequence is defined. SRS §18.3 lists the questions and M11 requires sign-off, so traceability is partial.* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: SRS §0 now defines owner sign-off recorded as dated `docs/DECISIONS.md` entries, with unconfirmed items listed as milestone risks and M11 requiring confirmation.*
- [ ] CHK016 - Are decisions that supersede earlier decisions explicitly marked as superseding, so a reader does not apply a stale rule? [Consistency, Gap] — *OPEN: supersession is implied by later text but no row says "supersedes DEC-nn", so a reader comparing two rows cannot tell which is current.*
- [ ] CHK017 - Are there conflicting pairs among DEC entries — for example DEC-16 (fines persist across payments) vs POL-08 (final amount fixed at return)? [Conflict, Spec DEC-16 vs POL-08] — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_2026-10-25.md`: POL-08 now defines per-Charge `days_from`/`days_to`/`rate`, final fine = Σ(days×rate) capped, top-up Charge for missed nights.*
- [ ] CHK018 - Is each `[+]` decision distinguishable from `[PA1]`-derived ones in a way that tells the reviewer which may be freely changed? [Clarity, Spec §3] — *PASS: `[+]` tags spec-added requirements; the preamble defines them as changeable by the owner.*

## Policy Quality (POL-01 … POL-17)

- [ ] CHK019 - Does every policy define its scope (who it applies to, which entity, which lifecycle stage)? [Completeness, Spec §4] — *PASS: each POL names its subject (accounts, membership, checkout, fines, receipts, etc.) and its trigger. Scope is generally evident from the rule text.*
- [ ] CHK020 - Are all numeric thresholds in policies expressed as settings keys rather than inline literals, with the literal only as a default? [Consistency, Spec §4.17, Constitution Principle VII] — *PASS: §4.17 is the single settings table and policies reference keys (e.g. `premium_fee_per_7_days`). Inline numbers appear only as defaults. Constitution Principle VII enforces it.*
- [ ] CHK021 - Is "day" defined for every policy that counts days (overdue days, reservation strike window, retention), including the timezone and inclusive/exclusive boundary? [Clarity, Spec §4.1, DEC-47] — *PASS: POL-01 fixes the timezone and POL-08 defines an overdue day as each local calendar day after due date. Strike window is a rolling 180 days (DEC-25). Retention periods (POL-16) are calendar durations; boundary not stated but non-critical.*
- [ ] CHK022 - Does POL-04 define the outcome when checkout partially fails for reasons other than availability (e.g. limit reached mid-transaction)? [Coverage, Spec §4.4] — *PASS: POL-04 states checkout is all-or-nothing, lists each failure, keeps the cart, and lets the student remove failed lines and retry. Applies to all failure kinds, not only availability.*
- [ ] CHK023 - Is the interaction defined between POL-04 (cancel allowed for `ready_for_pickup`) and POL-07 (a promoted reservation also enters `ready_for_pickup`)? [Conflict, Spec §4.4 vs §4.7] — *Resolved: a ready reservation holds only a Reservation row until handover; Loan Item materializes as `borrowed` (`source=reservation`).*
- [ ] CHK024 - Does POL-06 (renewal) state what happens when a renewal would cross the lost threshold or exceed the fine cap? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §4.6, §4.8] — *OPEN: POL-06 does not say whether renewal is blocked when the new due date would exceed the cap or approach lost conversion. Low risk (renewal extends, so it cannot immediately exceed), but unstated.*
- [ ] CHK025 - Is the reservation queue behavior when a book's last copy is retired or marked lost (queue never satisfiable) defined? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §4.7, §4.13] — *OPEN: EC-27 says such a book is not reservable, but §4.7/§5.3 do not say what happens to an existing queue when the last copy is retired or lost. Genuine gap.* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: POL-07 defines non-circulating books, cancels `waiting` reservations with reason `book_not_circulating` and no strike, and POL-13 runs the rule on slip completion.*
- [ ] CHK026 - Is the "one active loan of the same Book" rule (POL-04) reconciled with the reservation rule that a member may hold a ready reservation for a book they already have on loan? [Conflict, Spec §4.4 vs §4.7] — *Resolved: POL-07/FR-RES-01 now forbid reserving a book the member already holds (returns `DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_LOAN`).*
- [ ] CHK027 - Does POL-08 define whether the fine cap is computed per Loan Item or per Book, and does it match FR-LOAN-08's wording? [Ambiguity, Spec §4.8] — *PASS (after revision): POL-08 now says the cap applies to "the total of all fine Charges of the loan", and CHK017 clarifies the final fine basis. Wording is per-loan, consistent with FR-LOAN-08.*
- [ ] CHK028 - Is the lost-resolution refund window (90 days) applicable from loss date or payment date, and is that stated? [Ambiguity, Spec §4.8, settings `lost_return_refund_window_days`] — *OPEN: POL-08 says "within 90 days of loss", which reads as the loss date, but the setting name (`lost_return_refund_window_days`) does not fix the anchor. Worth one explicit clause.*
- [ ] CHK029 - Are debt-hold semantics unambiguous about whether a waived charge clears the hold immediately in the same transaction? [Clarity, Spec §4.9, FR-LOAN-07] — *PASS: FR-LOAN-07 requires `debt_outstanding` to update "in the same transaction as any charge or payment change", which covers a waiver.*
- [ ] CHK030 - Does POL-10 define behavior when a reversal would drive a receipt's net to a value outside the original payment (e.g. reversal after partial manual correction)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §4.10] — *PASS: POL-10 says a receipt is reversed once, fully, and partial corrections use a reversal plus a new manual receipt. That bounds the net-value question.*
- [ ] CHK031 - Is the manual-receipt "type" enumerated, or left open enough to become inconsistent with POL-10's receipt type list? [Clarity, Spec §4.10] — *OPEN: POL-10 enumerates receipt types but describes manual receipts only as "type (for example `replacement_fee`)", so the manual type set is open. Minor; a closed enum would remove the ambiguity.*
- [ ] CHK032 - Does POL-16 define retention for ledger rows belonging to an anonymized account, given "ledger rows keep a pseudonymous reference"? [Completeness, Spec §4.16] — *PASS: POL-16 gives 7-year retention for receipts/charges and says ledger rows keep a pseudonymous reference after anonymization, which resolves the overlap.*

## State Machine Completeness (§5)

- [ ] CHK033 - Is every Loan Item state in §5.2 reachable from `(new)` and does every path terminate in a documented terminal state? [Completeness, Spec §5.2] — *PASS: §5.2 lists transitions from `(new)` for every entry path and names terminal states explicitly (including the revised `lost` rule).*
- [ ] CHK034 - Does §5.2 define the transition for a `ready_for_pickup` item whose copy is discovered damaged before handover? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §5.2] — *OPEN: §5.2 has no transition for a `ready_for_pickup` item whose copy is found damaged pre-handover. SRS §20.6 archives the swap/cancel feature, so the documented answer is "out of scope", but §5.2 does not say so (EC-12 mentions it for holds).* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: §5.2 now has a `ready_for_pickup` row for a copy found damaged pre-handover, and EC-12 is rewritten.*
- [ ] CHK035 - Is "`lost` is terminal only after admin verification" reconciled with the `lost` → `returned` transition in the same table? [Conflict, Spec §5.2] — *Resolved: `lost_resolved_at` set at settlement (path A returns it, path B keeps it `lost`); restore checklist now checks "no `lost` with empty `lost_resolved_at`".*
- [ ] CHK036 - Are the side effects in §5.2 stated as requirements (testable), not as implementation notes? [Measurability, Spec §5.2] — *PASS: side effects are concrete observable outcomes (copy status, deadlines, receipts) rather than code detail.*
- [ ] CHK037 - Does §5.3 define what happens to a `waiting` reservation when the Book becomes non-circulating (all copies retired/lost)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §5.3, EC-27] — *OPEN: same gap as CHK025 — EC-27 covers reservability but §5.3 does not state what happens to a `waiting` reservation if the book stops circulating.* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: §5.3 now includes `waiting` → `cancelled` with reason `book_not_circulating`, no strike (POL-07).*
- [ ] CHK038 - Is every Copy transition in §5.4 attributed to a permitted actor, and is any transition reachable by more than one actor in a way that needs a precedence rule? [Consistency, Spec §5.4] — *PASS: every §5.4 row names its actor/by-column, and no transition is reachable by two actors in a conflicting way.*
- [ ] CHK039 - Is the `held` → `lost` transition addressed, given `held` copies can be flagged missing during an audit? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §5.4] — *OPEN: §5.4 has no `held` → `lost` row. CONFIRM-03 blocks write-off of held copies and EC-13 requires releasing the hold first, so the intended answer is "not allowed", but the table does not state it.* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: §5.4 now states `held` → `lost` is not a direct transition (release the hold first), and FR-INV-07 enforces it.*
- [ ] CHK040 - Are "other state sets" in §5.5 defined with the same rigor as the main machines, or do Suggestion/Batch/Slip defer entirely to policies without stating transitions? [Completeness, Spec §5.5] — *OPEN: §5.5 gives Suggestion/Batch/Slip as bare status enumerations with a pointer to POL-12/13, not full transition tables. Adequate for a summary but weaker than §5.2–§5.4.*
- [ ] CHK041 - Is the Payment state machine consistent with the refund rule in POL-05/DEC-11 (succeeded → refunded) and with `expired` for window expiry? [Consistency, Spec §5.5 vs §4.5] — *PASS: §5.5 Payment states include `succeeded`, `refunded`, and `expired`, matching POL-05/DEC-11 and DEC-13.*

## Gating Matrix (§6)

- [ ] CHK042 - Does every gated action in §6.1 correspond to at least one FR that enforces it? [Traceability, Spec §6.1] — *PASS: every row maps to an FR (FR-AUTH-05 gating, FR-RES-01, FR-LOAN-03, FR-SRCH-06, FR-MEM-02, FR-SUGG-01, FR-LOAN-06, FR-CIRC-02/03).*
- [ ] CHK043 - Is the precedence defined when multiple blockers apply simultaneously (e.g. Restricted + debt hold), including which error reason is returned? [Ambiguity, Spec §6.1, §8] — *OPEN: §6.1 defines the allowed/blocked cells but not precedence when two blockers apply (Restricted + debt hold), and §8 lists reasons without a priority order. Genuine ambiguity, low-risk but affects error UX and tests.* — *Resolved by `SPEC_REVISIONS_ver2_2026-10-25.md`: §6.1 now defines blocker precedence (account status → debt hold → reservation ban → not-member → limit) returning the first matching reason; FR-AUTH-05 carries it.*
- [ ] CHK044 - Is the "Non-member" column consistent with POL-03's entitlement table (reserve = No for non-member, but §6.1 shows Reserve blocked)? [Consistency, Spec §6.1 vs §4.3] — *Resolved (not a conflict): §6.1 now states the column is derived from entitlements (FR-MEM-05), not hard-coded.*
- [ ] CHK045 - Is the behavior defined for an admin acting on behalf of a blocked student (e.g. handover while the student has debt)? [Clarity, Spec §6.1] — *PASS: FR-CIRC-02 explicitly refuses handover when debt > 0 or status is not active, with a specific reason, which is the admin-on-behalf case.*
- [ ] CHK046 - Is "pending verification" reachable only pre-activation, and does §6.1 cover the case of a user whose verification was revoked? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §6.1] — *OPEN: §6.1 covers `pending_verification`, but "revoked verification" is not a modeled state (POL-02 has no such transition). Probably effectively impossible; worth confirming.*

## Non-Functional Requirements (§7)

- [ ] CHK047 - Is every NFR expressed as a measurable target with a stated operating condition (load, device, network)? [Measurability, Spec §7] — *PASS (mostly): NFR-01 states device/network, NFR-02 states corpus size, NFR-03 states p95 per operation, NFR-05 states scale. NFR-04 and NFR-06..16 are qualitative or reference other docs.*
- [ ] CHK048 - Are NFR-01 and NFR-04 free of implementation words ("bundle", "API requests") that belong in the plan rather than the requirement? [Clarity, Spec §7] — *OPEN: NFR-01 says "initial JS ≤ 250 KB gzip" and NFR-04 says "≤ 12 API requests"; both are implementation-shaped. Legitimate as budgets, but they read as plan constraints. Low severity — flag for the plan stage.*
- [ ] CHK049 - Is NFR-10 ("see SRS") expanded enough to be verifiable from this document alone, or is the delegation acceptable and recorded? [Traceability, Spec §7] — *OPEN: NFR-10 is literally "see SRS". The invariants live in SRS §13/NFR-10 and the nightly reconciliation; core does not restate them. Delegation is deliberate but not marked as such in §7.*
- [ ] CHK050 - Does an NFR cover availability/degradation for the scheduled jobs specifically, distinct from the 99.5% API target? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §7, NFR-09] — *OPEN: NFR-09 mentions "idempotent mutations/jobs, retries with backoff" and "alerts on job failure", so job reliability is partly covered, but there is no distinct availability/latency target for the job pipeline itself. Genuine but low-risk gap.*
- [ ] CHK051 - Is the accessibility target (WCAG 2.2 AA) mapped to at least one verifiable acceptance condition per critical flow? [Coverage, Spec §7, NFR-08] — *OPEN: NFR-08 lists WCAG 2.2 AA properties (focus, contrast, 44 px, aria-live, reduced motion), and NT-04 defines axe-core CI checks plus manual keyboard/screen-reader runs. Mapping exists at the NFR/NT level but not per critical flow (register, search, checkout, pay, return).*
- [ ] CHK052 - Is data-retention (POL-16) reflected as an NFR, or only as a policy, and is the consistency between them stated? [Consistency, Spec §4.16 vs §7] — *PASS: POL-16 is the retention rule; NFR-07 (Privacy) explicitly references POL-16, so the two are linked rather than duplicated.*
- [ ] CHK053 - Are cost-control requirements (NFR-15) given a defined fallback behavior and a measurable trigger? [Clarity, Spec §7, NFR-15] — *PASS: NFR-15 defines a monthly cap with automatic fallback to a degraded mode, and NT-07 tests budget exhaustion switching to fallback.*

## Data Model & Error Contract (§8)

- [ ] CHK054 - Is every named error reason in §8 mapped to exactly one HTTP status and one user-facing meaning? [Completeness, Spec §8] — *PASS: §8 groups every reason under exactly one status code (400/401/403/404/409/410/422/429/500), and the UI-maps-reason rule is stated.*
- [ ] CHK055 - Are error reasons used by the gating matrix present in the error contract (DEBT_HOLD, RESERVATION_BAN, NOT_MEMBER, ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED)? [Consistency, Spec §6.1 vs §8] — *PASS: all four appear in §8's 403 list.*
- [ ] CHK056 - Is `STATUS_CHANGED` defined with the guarantee that it carries current state, and is that guarantee testable? [Measurability, Spec §8] — *PASS: §8 says `STATUS_CHANGED` "always carries the current status" so the UI can refresh; that is directly testable (assert the payload contains current status).*
- [ ] CHK057 - Is the data model summary explicit that it is non-normative and that §12 of the SRS is authoritative, avoiding two competing schemas? [Clarity, Spec §8] — *PASS: §8 opens by stating full detail is in SRS §12 and that core is a summary; feature specs reference entities by name.*
- [ ] CHK058 - Is there a requirement that the receipt-number format `RC-<YYYY>-<6 digit>` is unique and gap-free per year, stated in the core rather than only in the receipts spec? [Traceability, Spec §4.10 vs 009-receipts] — *PASS: the receipt-number format and the `FOR UPDATE` gap-free rule are stated in POL-10 (§4.10) and referenced by FR-RCPT-01.*

## Scenario Coverage, Edge Cases & Recovery

- [ ] CHK059 - Are exception/error scenarios represented at core level, or does every core rule assume the happy path with errors delegated to feature specs? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §4, §5] — *OPEN: core policies are mostly happy-path; error/exception behavior lives in EC-01..EC-36 (SRS §15.2) and the §8 error contract. §4/§5 rarely state failure behavior inline. Deliberate split, but a reader of core alone would not know errors exist.*
- [ ] CHK060 - Are recovery/rollback requirements defined for a mutation that commits but whose notification side effect fails? [Coverage, Gap, Exception Flow] — *PASS: NFR-09 requires retries with backoff, and POL-11/`email_outbox` model retry and `failed` states with in-app fallback, so a committed mutation with a failed notification is covered.*
- [ ] CHK061 - Is the behavior defined when a scheduled job runs late across a state boundary (e.g. nightly run after a handover already occurred)? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §4.8] — *PASS (after revision): POL-18 and EC-35 state jobs process everything due and deadlines are re-checked at action time, so a late job cannot double-apply. EC-03 covers the handover/hold-expiry race.*
- [ ] CHK062 - Are concurrency requirements stated as invariants (must-never-happen) rather than procedures, so they can be verified independently of implementation? [Measurability, Spec §4.4, NFR-10] — *PASS: NFR-10 states invariants as must-hold equalities (a copy held by at most one item; counters equal counts; debt equals sum), which are verifiable by the nightly reconciliation.*
- [ ] CHK063 - Is the set of global edge cases referenced (EC-01…EC-36) derivable from core alone, or does the reader have no way to know which EC applies to which rule? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §9] — *OPEN: §9 only points at SRS §15.2; there is no mapping from EC to the policy it qualifies. Feature specs list their own ECs, which partly mitigates. Real traceability gap for a core-level reader.*
- [ ] CHK064 - Is the behavior for a clock/timezone change (e.g. server region, DST-free assumption violated) addressed? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §4.1, DEC-55] — *OPEN: POL-01 fixes `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` and DEC-55 says UTC+7 no DST; no rule covers what happens if that assumption is broken (region migration, DST introduction). Low risk, but unstated.*

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Risks

- [ ] CHK065 - Is every assumption (ASM-01…ASM-10) tied to at least one requirement that would break if it were false? [Traceability, Spec §11] — *OPEN: ASM-01..ASM-10 are listed but not linked to the requirements they underpin (e.g. ASM-04 identity → FR-AUTH-01/02; ASM-01 scale → NFR-05). The linkage is inferable but not written.*
- [ ] CHK066 - Are external dependencies (LLM, embedding, email, ISBN lookup) given a stated failure mode at core level, not only in feature specs? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §11] — *OPEN: core §11/§3 mention the dependencies (DEC-34 ISBN, DEC-45/54 Supabase, ASM-07 LLM keys) but failure modes live in feature specs (FR-AI-07) and SRS §10.3. Not stated at core level.*
- [ ] CHK067 - Is the open-questions list (§11) resolved or explicitly deferred with an owner, rather than left as a flat list? [Completeness, Spec §11] — *OPEN: core §11 delegates to SRS §18.3, which is a flat numbered list of 13 questions with no owner or resolution status.*
- [ ] CHK068 - Is the single-staff-role decision (DEC-01) consistent with the permission matrix, and does the matrix avoid implying capabilities that a future split role would change? [Consistency, Spec §2.3 vs DEC-01] — *PASS: DEC-01 explicitly states one staff role covers both; §2.3 has a single admin column and a note that the two-role design is archived.*

## Build Order & Definition of Done

- [ ] CHK069 - Does every milestone M0–M11 have exit criteria that are objectively checkable, not just a list of FR groups? [Measurability, Spec §10] — *PASS: each milestone names explicit TS/NT scenarios as exit criteria (e.g. M1 requires TS-01..06, TS-41, TS-42, TS-60).*
- [ ] CHK070 - Is every FR assigned to exactly one milestone, with no FR appearing in two milestones or none? [Completeness, Spec §10] — *PASS: the M1–M11 scope column covers all 107 FRs, and spot checks show no FR in two milestones. (Worth an automated check in the spec-matrix script.)*
- [ ] CHK071 - Is the definition of done consistent with NFR-14's testing expectations and with the spec-matrix CI gate? [Consistency, Spec §10 vs §7] — *PASS: the definition of done requires the FR acceptance test, the TS scenario, and the spec-matrix check, matching NFR-14 (pgTAP, integration, Playwright) and the CI gate.*

## Ambiguities & Conflicts Requiring Resolution

- [ ] CHK072 - Is there a single authoritative rule for what counts as an "active item" (DEC-22), consistent across gating, membership expiry, and reservation promotion? [Ambiguity, Spec DEC-22, §4.3, DEC-26] — *PASS (after revision): DEC-22 defines the counted set once; §4.7's promotion check order now references DEC-22 for the limit, and DEC-23 uses the same counted items, so one definition is used throughout.*
- [ ] CHK073 - Are the two membership-expiry effects (DEC-23 non-member limit; DEC-26 promotion cancellation) reconcilable, or do they conflict for a member with loans at limit? [Conflict, Spec DEC-23 vs DEC-26] — *Resolved: POL-07 now fixes the promotion check order (account/debt/membership → duplicate active loan → item limit → promote).*
- [ ] CHK074 - Is the phrase "task need" in POL-16 (staff may view borrowing history) defined by a testable rule? [Ambiguity, Spec §4.16] — *OPEN: "staff with a task need" is still undefined. POL-16 does require an audit entry when staff open a student detail page, which makes access traceable but not restricted by a rule. Genuine ambiguity; low risk given only one staff role.*
- [ ] CHK075 - Is it clear whether settings changes apply to in-flight transactions or only to transactions starting after commit? [Ambiguity, Spec §4.17, EC-07] — *Resolved: new POL-18 (§4.19) defines stored-vs-live settings timing; EC-07 now references it.*

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Items 017, 023, 026, 035, 044, 073 flag suspected conflicts between core rules; these are the highest-value items to resolve before planning
